subject: Science
title: Reading a Line Graph
standardTag: SCI.D.3 — Interpret data presented in graphs and tables
tipLine: Start by reading both axis labels before you look at the line itself.

vocabTerms.definition: something that can change or be changed, and is measured in an experiment
the general direction data moves over time — up, down, or flat

blocks.heading: What the axes tell you
blocks.body: A line graph shows how one variable changes in relation to another. The horizontal axis (x-axis) usually shows time or another independent variable. The vertical axis (y-axis) shows the value being measured. Always check the units on each axis before drawing conclusions.

blocks.heading: Spotting a trend
blocks.body: A trend is the general direction the data moves — rising, falling, or staying flat. A single data point can be misleading, but a trend across many points tells you something real is happening. Look at the overall shape of the line, not just the start and end points.

blocks.question: A graph shows a plant's height measured every week for two months, and the line rises steadily each week. What does this line represent?
options: A single measurement of the plant
A trend of increasing height over time
The units used to measure height
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — a steady rise across many weeks is a trend, not just one data point.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite — one rising line across many weeks shows a trend (increasing height over time), not a single measurement.

blocks.question: Before drawing any conclusion from a line graph, what should you check first?
options: The labels and units on both axes
How long the graph took to make
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — axis labels and units tell you what's actually being measured.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite — always check the labels and units on both axes first, so you know what the graph is actually measuring.
